# BayCounty.me: every page and dataset

> BayCounty.me is a free, independent guide to the public records of Bay County, Florida: its county, cities, school district and special districts. It shows where tax money goes, budgets, contracts and the vendors paid, how officials voted, campaign money, meetings, elections, public notices, schools, restaurant inspections, emergencies and more, each figure linked to its government source.

## How to read this site

- Every number links to the public record it came from (budgets, audits, minutes, state and federal filings). /data-sources lists each source and how often it is read.
- The site covers 2016 to today. Earlier years are not included.
- Individual campaign donors are not named; gifts are summed. The exception is a donor who runs a registered business, listed by name with their businesses. Home addresses are never shown.
- Salaries are named only for elected officials and department leaders.
- Corrections: /about explains how to report one; each fix is logged on /updates.

## En español

- [Registros públicos en español](https://baycounty.me/es): BayCounty.me en español: estimado de impuestos por dirección, solicitudes de registros públicos y un glosario de términos de dinero público.
- [Quiénes son candidatos en 2026](https://baycounty.me/es/elecciones): Cada contienda local en las boletas del condado de Bay en 2026: los candidatos, sus propuestas, enlaces a sus campañas y de dónde viene el dinero de su campaña.
- [Exenciones del impuesto a la propiedad](https://baycounty.me/es/exenciones): Quién recibe una exención del impuesto a la propiedad en el condado de Bay, desde el homestead hasta los veteranos con discapacidad, cuántas casas y cuánto impuesto quita cada una, según el registro de 2026.
- [Glosario en lenguaje sencillo](https://baycounty.me/es/glosario): Cada término de BayCounty.me explicado de forma sencilla: CRA, incremento de impuestos, millaje, exención de vivienda principal, presupuestos y más.
- [A dónde va su impuesto a la propiedad](https://baycounty.me/es/impuestos): Calcule su factura del impuesto a la propiedad en el condado de Bay y vea qué parte recibe cada gobierno, de dónde saca el resto de su dinero y en qué lo gasta.
- [Mi dirección](https://baycounty.me/es/mi-direccion): Busque cualquier dirección del condado de Bay: estimado de impuestos a la propiedad, quién lo representa, escuelas, zonas de inundación y evacuación, y distritos de reurbanización.
- [Próximas reuniones públicas en el condado de Bay](https://baycounty.me/es/reuniones): Cuándo y dónde se reúnen la Comisión del Condado, la Junta Escolar y cada comisión de ciudad, con enlaces a las agendas y los temas de dinero de cada una.
- [Solicite un registro público](https://baycounty.me/es/solicitar-registros): Escriba una solicitud de registros públicos de Florida a cualquier gobierno del condado de Bay en un minuto.
- [Tarifas en su factura de impuestos, y facturas de servicios](https://baycounty.me/es/tarifas-y-facturas): Las tarifas fijas de bomberos, aguas pluviales y otras en las facturas de impuestos del condado de Bay, y una factura típica de agua, alcantarillado y basura en cada ciudad.

## Other pages

- [Bay County public records, mapped](https://baycounty.me/): Maps, money and public records for Bay County, Florida, with a source on every figure.
- [Ask BayCounty.me](https://baycounty.me/ask): Ask a question in your own words about Bay County budgets, taxes, votes, contracts, meetings or officials, and get an answer from the public records on BayCounty.me, with links to each source.
- [IRONMAN Florida race week: road closures and where to watch](https://baycounty.me/events/ironman-florida): IRONMAN Florida in Panama City Beach, Saturday, November 7, 2026: a live map of every road closure, hour by hour through race week, the race schedule, the swim, bike and run course, where to watch and how to get around.
- [Privacy](https://baycounty.me/privacy): What BayCounty.me and its iPhone and Android apps collect: no ads, no tracking, and optional accounts for your home and for the realtor console.
- [Search](https://baycounty.me/search): Search every page, glossary term and public-money record on BayCounty.me.

## Datasets

Catalog: https://baycounty.me/downloads/index.json. API: https://baycounty.me/api/v1/datasets/<id> (filters, sort, paging; see https://baycounty.me/developers).

### Government profiles (government-profiles)
One row per government: population, budget, tax rate, debt, audit findings, votes, staff, utility bill and Hurricane Michael money.
Rows: 9. Columns: government, kind, population_2025, budget_total, general_fund, budget_status, millage, property_tax_levy, debt_total, debt_year, audit_year, audit_findings, repeat_findings, votes_recorded, split_votes, employees_fte, typical_utility_bill, fema_michael_obligated, page, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/government-profiles.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/government-profiles.json

### Recorded votes (votes)
Votes by the County Commission, School Board, city commissions and CRA boards since 2016, with how each member voted: hand-researched money votes plus every motion read from the official minutes.
Rows: 11,802. Columns: date, government, board, category, headline, summary, amount, outcome, tally, split, voted_yes, voted_no, absent_or_abstained, agenda_item, source_title, source_url, members, source_type, verified, vote_method, mover, seconder, source_page, vote_id, contract_ids, contract_match_method, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/votes.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/votes.json

### Votes by member (member-votes)
One row per member per vote (long format), for tallying individual records.
Rows: 57,166. Columns: date, board, member, vote, headline, source_url, gov_id, source_type, vote_id, person_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/member-votes.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/member-votes.json

### Contracts (contracts)
Major contracts approved since October 2022: vendor, amount, purpose, how awarded.
Rows: 391. Columns: government, vendor, amount, purpose, date, method, source_title, source_url, notes, record_id, vote_ids, vote_match_method, vendor_id, vendor_ids, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/contracts.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/contracts.json

### Change orders (change-orders)
Contract change orders with original and new totals.
Rows: 55. Columns: government, vendor, project, original_amount, change_amount, new_total, pct_of_original, reason, date, source_url, record_id, vote_ids, vote_match_method, vendor_id, vendor_ids, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/change-orders.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/change-orders.json

### Emergency purchases (emergency-purchases)
Purchases made under emergency rules without normal bidding.
Rows: 12. Columns: government, vendor, amount, purpose, date, basis, source_url, record_id, vote_ids, vote_match_method, vendor_id, vendor_ids, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/emergency-purchases.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/emergency-purchases.json

### CRA spending (cra-payments)
What Bay County's Community Redevelopment Agencies paid for, with locations.
Rows: 144. Columns: cra, city, payee, amount, date_or_fy, status, category, purpose, location_name, district, lat, lng, count, source_title, source_url, notes, payee_entity_id, vendor_id, vendor_ids, gov_id, date_start, date_end, date_precision
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/cra-payments.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/cra-payments.json

### Property tax rates (property-tax-rates)
Millage, rolled-back rate and levy for every taxing authority, by tax year.
Rows: 105. Columns: authority_id, authority, kind, school, tax_year, millage, rolled_back_rate, levy, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/property-tax-rates.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/property-tax-rates.json

### Debt by government (debt)
Total debt from the latest audited financial statements.
Rows: 13. Columns: government, fy, total_debt, total_debt_note, population_2025_estimate, source_url, gov_id, date_start, date_end, date_precision
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/debt.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/debt.json

### Audit findings (audit-findings)
Findings from audits filed with the Florida Auditor General, in plain English.
Rows: 106. Columns: government, fy, opinion, finding, plain_english, repeat, management_response, source_url, gov_id, date_start, date_end, date_precision
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/audit-findings.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/audit-findings.json

### Hurricane Michael FEMA projects (fema-michael-projects)
Every FEMA Public Assistance project in Bay County for disaster DR-4399.
Rows: 765. Columns: applicant, project, title, category, federal_share, eligible_amount, first_obligated, last_obligated, status, size, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/fema-michael-projects.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/fema-michael-projects.json

### Half-cent sales tax projects (sales-tax-projects)
Every infrastructure sales tax project on the county map, with status and cost. schedule_* columns add the county program schedule's programmed dollars by year where the schedule line could be matched to the project.
Rows: 1,062. Columns: name, government, category, status, pct_complete, promised_cost, programmed_cost, actual_cost, fiscal_years, location, lat, lng, description, source_url, schedule_programmed_total, schedule_fy_amounts, schedule_line, schedule_match_method, schedule_source_url, gov_id, date_start, date_end, date_precision
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/sales-tax-projects.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/sales-tax-projects.json

### Tourist tax collections (bed-tax-collections)
Bed tax collected by zone and fiscal year. A partial year (the current one) also gives prior_year_same_period: what was collected over the same months a year earlier, from the same Clerk report.
Rows: 33. Columns: fy, district, amount, partial, period, prior_year_same_period, basis, source_url, gov_id, date_start, date_end, date_precision
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/bed-tax-collections.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/bed-tax-collections.json

### Fees on tax bills (fees-assessments)
Non-ad valorem assessments: fire, stormwater, CRA and other flat fees.
Rows: 18. Columns: government, area, name, category, how_charged, rate, residential_single_family_amount, fiscal_year, source_url, gov_id, date_start, date_end, date_precision
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/fees-assessments.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/fees-assessments.json

### Officials and pay (officials-pay)
Salaries of top elected and appointed officials. Rows with row_type board_total are a whole board's combined pay, not one person.
Rows: 33. Columns: government, title, name, annual, year, basis, source_url, row_type, district, person_id, gov_id, date_start, date_end, date_precision
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/officials-pay.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/officials-pay.json

### Accountability: projects (accountability-projects)
One row per project on the Accountability console: stage, first and latest figures, cost growth, questions raised by the published rules, records still missing and the agency reply.
Rows: 97. Columns: project_id, project, government, agency, kind, stage, first_figure, first_figure_is, latest_figure, latest_figure_is, growth_pct, project_total, flags, records_missing, agency_reply, first_date, last_date, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/accountability-projects.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/accountability-projects.json

### Accountability: project timelines (accountability-events)
Every dated event in each project timeline: budgets, approvals, awards, change orders, votes, payments and completion, with sources.
Rows: 250. Columns: project_id, project, government, date, sort_date, event, amount, approximate, description, paid_to, news_report, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/accountability-events.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/accountability-events.json

### Connections: payees (connections-payees)
Every payee in the payment records of every local government and agency (contracts, change orders, emergency purchases, check registers, tourism agency payments and the CRA ledger) as one entity, with who paid it and whether it gave to a campaign. dollars_in_records adds every record, and an award and the payments on it can both be records, so it is not a deduplicated total. Unnamed grant recipients are grouped.
Rows: 656. Columns: entity_id, name, kind, subconsultant_only, paid_by, record_types, records, dollars_in_records, gave_to_campaigns, vendor_page, nonprofit_id, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/connections-payees.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/connections-payees.json

### Connections: payment records (connections-payments)
One row per payment record behind the Connections network: which government or agency paid which payee, the record type, amount, date and source. CRA ledger items that are only proposed or planned are not included.
Rows: 1,182. Columns: record_id, payer_id, payer, payer_kind, payer_gov_id, entity_id, payee, record_type, amount, date, what, cra_status, inside_project_total, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/connections-payments.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/connections-payments.json

### Connections: documented links (connections-links)
Documented links between payees that are not payments (shared project, address or subcontract), each with its source.
Rows: 6. Columns: entity_a, name_a, entity_b, name_b, connection, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/connections-links.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/connections-links.json

### Connections: business gifts to officials (connections-gifts)
Gifts from businesses, PACs and committees to current officeholders and 2026 candidates, one row per donor and official, with the payee id when the donor was also paid by a local government. Individual donors are never included.
Rows: 2,685. Columns: donor, donor_type, official, office, official_gov_id, candidate_2026, past_campaign_year, sits_on, amount, gifts, dates, payee_entity_id, match_confidence, report_url, as_of, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/connections-gifts.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/connections-gifts.json

### Money map: gifts to officials (money-map-gifts)
Gifts from businesses and committees to each current officeholder, and whether the donor holds contracts with that official's government. Individuals appear only as totals.
Rows: 548. Columns: donor, donor_type, official, office, gov, amount, dates, donor_holds_contracts_here, official_total_raised, official_from_individuals, official_individual_gifts, report_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/money-map-gifts.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/money-map-gifts.json

### Money map: donor contracts (money-map-contracts)
Contracts, awards and payments held by campaign donors, per donor and government.
Rows: 60. Columns: donor, donor_type, gov, government, awarded_total, paid_total, awards, other_records, records, source_urls, likely_match_only, vendor, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/money-map-contracts.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/money-map-contracts.json

### Money map: votes on donors' contracts (money-map-votes)
Recorded votes by an official on a contract with one of their own donors, with the gift dates and whether the gifts came before the vote, after it, or both (column gift_before_or_after_vote: before, after, before and after).
Rows: 18. Columns: donor, official, office, gov, gift_amount, gift_dates, vote_date, item, amount, vote, outcome, tally, consent_agenda, gift_before_or_after_vote, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/money-map-votes.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/money-map-votes.json

### Donors with government contracts (donor-contracts)
Each business donor matched to a local government contract, award or payment, with the match method and confidence.
Rows: 211. Columns: contributor, vendor_name, vendor_id, candidate, person_id, office, office_gov_id, election, contribution_amount, contribution_dates, refunded_by_campaign, match_confidence, note, campaign_report_url, same_government_as_office, vendor, contract_ids_or_descriptions, record_ids, contract_source_urls, contract_government, contract_gov_id, contract_governments, contract_gov_ids, record_types, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/donor-contracts.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/donor-contracts.json

### Companies (vendors-directory)
Every company in BayCounty.me records, with its other spellings, the governments it works with and how many records name it.
Rows: 608. Columns: vendor_id, name, aliases, gov_ids, records, vendor_type, page, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/vendors-directory.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/vendors-directory.json

### People (people-directory)
Elected officials, department leaders and 2026 candidates named in BayCounty.me records, with their roles. sort_order is the People page's order: by the government they are listed under (primary_gov_id), then title (title_rank 0 mayor, chair or elected officer to 8 past candidate, named in title_group), then last name. status is current (in office, on staff or on the 2026 ballot) or past (former officials and past candidates).
Rows: 321. Columns: person_id, name, district, gov_ids, roles, primary_gov_id, title_rank, title_group, status, sort_order, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/people-directory.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/people-directory.json

### Glossary (glossary-terms)
Plain-English definitions of the government and tax terms used on the site.
Rows: 45. Columns: term_id, group_id, group_name, term, simple, more, example, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/glossary-terms.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/glossary-terms.json

### What's new (site-updates)
Each change to the site's data and pages, newest first.
Rows: 67. Columns: date, title, text, pages, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/site-updates.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/site-updates.json

### Savings finder: opportunities (savings-opportunities)
Places Bay County governments could spend less: the spending each touches, a low and high estimate with its stated assumption, the next step and the records still needed. Every figure is computed from the Accountability projects and the CRA ledger.
Rows: 10. Columns: opportunity_id, rank, title, government, gov_ids, lever, confidence, in_play, in_play_is, rate_low, rate_high, savings_low, savings_high, estimate, basis, assumption, next_step, overlaps, records_needed, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/savings-opportunities.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/savings-opportunities.json

### Savings finder: evidence (savings-evidence)
The records behind each savings opportunity, one row per project or CRA ledger record: the figure, what it is compared with, the gap or share, cost per unit where one applies, and the source.

### Governments by year (government-years)
One row per government per fiscal year: adopted budget and its status, general fund, property tax rate and levy, audited actual revenue and spending, residents, audited debt and staff count. A blank means no record for that year. fiscal_year is the year the fiscal year ends (FY2026 = Oct 2025 to Sep 2026; schools Jul to Jun).
Rows: 103. Columns: gov_id, government, fiscal_year, fy, period, budget_total, general_fund, budget_status, budget_note, budget_excludes_transfers, budget_source_url, tax_year, millage, rolled_back_rate, property_tax_levy, millage_source_url, actual_revenue, actual_spending, actuals_source_url, population, population_year, population_source, debt_total, debt_source_url, employees_fte, employees_note, employees_source_url, budget_per_resident, source_url, date_start, date_end, date_precision
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/government-years.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/government-years.json

### Budgets by year, line by line (budget-years)
Every budget line on record for each government and fiscal year, to compare one year with another. basis adopted: the adopted budget's total and General Fund, each fund and each General Fund department. basis actual: audited revenue by source and spending by function from the state's Local Government Financial Reports (in_total is false for transfers and borrowing, which the audited totals leave out). line_key lines the same fund or department up across years; service groups departments into common services. fiscal_year is the year the fiscal year ends (FY2026 = Oct 2025 to Sep 2026; schools Jul to Jun).
Rows: 2,377. Columns: gov_id, government, fiscal_year, fy, basis, section, line_key, name, service, fund_type, amount, in_total, status, source_url, date_start, date_end, date_precision

Each business that gave to a current officeholder or 2026 local candidate, matched to its Florida Division of Corporations (Sunbiz) record: document number, registered name, status and principal city, with the match method. Business-level only; no owner or officer names.

Type, IRS subsection, latest 990 revenue, expenses and assets, how many board members its filings list, how many of those sit on another local board, government payment records and grants. Board members are in nonprofit-board-members.

### Business officers (business-officers)
Officers, managers, members and the registered agent of each registered business that has a profile on BayCounty.me (a company paid by a local government, a campaign donor, a federal contractor, a restaurant license holder and others), as filed with the Florida Division of Corporations (Sunbiz). One row per person or company and title; names and titles only, never addresses. officer_entity_id links an officer who already has a profile tied to that business (a nonprofit board member or a business owner who gave to a campaign); entity_id is the business's profile.
Rows: 13,559. Columns: place_id, entity_id, sunbiz_doc_number, business, business_status, officer, title, officer_kind, officer_entity_id, source_url, gov_id

### Campaign gifts from business owners (owner-gifts)
Personal gifts to local campaigns from people who run a registered Florida business, one row per person and campaign. A contributor filed as an individual is listed when the name and street address on the Supervisor of Elections filing are the same as an officer, manager or registered agent of a for-profit business on Sunbiz that was active around the gift; middle initials and Jr/Sr must agree, and protected voters are never matched. Other individual donors are never named. No addresses or occupations.
Rows: 1,117. Columns: donor_id, donor, businesses, business_doc_numbers, active_businesses, candidate, candidate_id, office, election, gifts, amount, first_date, last_date, match, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/owner-gifts.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/owner-gifts.json

### Profiles: people, companies and organizations (entity-profiles)
Every company, elected official, candidate, nonprofit, nonprofit board member, registered business, committee and government named in BayCounty.me records, one row each, with its profile page and how many documented connections it has. entity_id (kind:key) joins entity-connections. Board members are named as their nonprofits' public filings list them; individual campaign donors are included only when they run a registered business (owner-gifts).
Rows: 16,720. Columns: entity_id, kind, kind_label, name, subtitle, page_url, aliases, connections, amount_received, amount_given, gov_id, county, source_url
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/entity-profiles.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/entity-profiles.json

### Connections between people, companies and organizations (entity-connections)
Every documented connection between two entities in entity-profiles, totalled per pair and kind: a government paid a payee, an organization gave to an official's or candidate's campaign, an official voted on a company's contracts, a person sits on a nonprofit's board or runs a business, a nonprofit gave a grant, two payees share a project. Each row has its source. Individual campaign donors are included only when they run a registered business (owner-gifts); officials' board seats and businesses are added by the API once checked by hand.
Rows: 22,843. Columns: link_id, from_id, from_name, from_kind, from_url, to_id, to_name, to_kind, to_url, relation, relation_label, amount, records, first_date, last_date, detail, source_url, county, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/entity-connections.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/entity-connections.json

### Officeholders by year (officeholder-terms)
Who held each elected seat, and each government's appointed manager, on every local government since 2016: one row per person per seat, with start_date and end_date, so the officials in office on any date or in any fiscal year can be picked out. person_name is blank for a known vacancy (vacant true) and for a stretch nobody could confirm from the records found (confirmed false); the note says which. start_date blank = in office before 2016; end_date blank = in office now. start_approx / end_approx mark dates known only to the month or year. appointed is true for the government's appointed manager or administrator (the county manager, city managers, Mexico Beach's administrator) and false for elected seats. how is elected, special election, appointed, interim or commission (chosen by the commission). Each term names its source: election results, minutes, budget books, city sites or news. place_id is the place (fl-bay = Bay County).
Rows: 162. Columns: place_id, gov_id, government, body, seat, seat_order, appointed, term_order, person_name, person_id, start_date, end_date, start_approx, end_approx, how, vacant, confirmed, note, source_title, source_url, date_start, date_end, date_precision
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/officeholder-terms.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/officeholder-terms.json

### Where the data comes from (data-sources)
Every source BayCounty.me takes records from, one row per source: the topic, the government it covers (or state and federal databases), the link, how we get it (automatic fetch, downloaded and read by hand, a state or federal bulk file, or a live lookup), how often, what we take from it, how we process it and the checks we run.
Rows: 187. Columns: topic, topic_id, government, government_id, source_name, source_url, method, refresh, what_we_take, how_we_process, checks, page, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/data-sources.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/data-sources.json

### Official photos (official-photos)
Official headshots of current elected officials and department leaders, one row per person: the photo on BayCounty.me (photo_url, a 320px square WebP), who published it (credit) and the government page it came from (source_url), and when it was copied. Only photos a government publishes on its own website; never campaign, news or social media photos. person_id joins officeholder-terms and entity_id joins entity-profiles. Anyone not listed has no published photo and is shown with initials.
Rows: 40. Columns: place_id, person_id, entity_id, name, photo_url, photo_path, width, height, credit, source_url, image_source_url, fetched_on, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/official-photos.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/official-photos.json

### Person photos (person-photos)
Every photo of a person on BayCounty.me, one row per profile: officials' headshots their government publishes (published_by government, same as official-photos) and chamber of commerce board and staff headshots the chamber publishes on its own site (published_by chamber). entity_id is the profile (person: for officials, member: for board members) and joins entity-profiles and chamber-leaders; person_id is set for officials. photo_url is the 320px square WebP BayCounty.me serves, credit who published it and source_url the page it came from. A government photo wins over a chamber photo for the same person. Anyone not listed is shown with initials.
Rows: 114. Columns: place_id, entity_id, person_id, name, photo_url, photo_path, published_by, credit, source_url, image_source_url, fetched_on, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/person-photos.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/person-photos.json

### How complete each government's data is (data-completeness)
For each government and each portion of its records (adopted budgets, audited spending, tax rates, debt, audit findings, officials by year): the years since 2016 we expect (period, expected), how many we have on file (have), the percent loaded (pct) and a status: complete (100%), partial (50-99%) or missing (under 50%). missing lists the fiscal years not on file. For officials, have and expected are seat-years and pct is the share where the officeholder is confirmed. Votes read from minutes change every few hours and are in /api/v1/import-progress instead.
Rows: 54. Columns: gov_id, government, portion_id, portion, period, have, expected, unit, pct, status, missing, detail, page_url, source_url
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/data-completeness.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/data-completeness.json

### Websites our records cite (data-source-sites)
Every website cited by the records behind BayCounty.me, per topic, with how many distinct documents and pages from it the data links to. Counted from the data files at each build.
Rows: 434. Columns: website, topic, topic_id, documents_cited, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/data-source-sites.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/data-source-sites.json

### Site menu (site-menu)
Every link in the site's main menu, one row per link, in English and Spanish: the section and the question it answers, the link's place in the section, and the section's start-here page. place_id is the place the menu belongs to (fl-bay = Bay County), so a menu for another place sits beside it.

### CRAs: tax increment by agency (cra-agencies)
One row per Community Redevelopment Agency that collects tax increment in Bay County: when it was created, its base year, the FY2025 increment and how much of it Bay County and the city paid, the total on record, its sunset date and what that date rests on, and the increment still to come under a 3%, 6% or 9% growth scenario. sunset_assumed is true where the CRA's plan was not found.
Rows: 7. Columns: cra_id, cra, gov_id, city, created, base_year, first_fy_on_record, years_filled, increment_fy2025, county_share_fy2025, county_fy2025, city_fy2025, paid_on_record, county_paid_on_record, sunset_fy, sunset_assumed, sunset_basis, yearly_cap, to_come_low, to_come_mid, to_come_high, source_url

### CRAs: tax increment by year (cra-tax-increment)
Property tax paid to each CRA by fiscal year, split between Bay County and the city by millage. scenario history: basis reported (from CRA reports, audits and budgets) or filled gap (between two reported years). scenario low, mid, high: FY2026 to the CRA's sunset, from adopted budgets where they exist, then 3%, 6% or 9% growth a year (Front Beach Road capped at $30M). Schools and the water management district are exempt and pay nothing.
Rows: 373. Columns: cra_id, cra, gov_id, fiscal_year, fy, basis, scenario, increment, county_share, county_amount, city_amount, source_url

Official county figures for CRA payments next to this estimate for the same year, with the difference in percent.

CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/cra-increment-checks.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/cra-increment-checks.json

### Chambers of commerce (chambers)
One row per chamber of commerce: what it is and who it serves, its board meetings, its latest IRS Form 990 (revenue, expenses, assets, employees), public money paid to it by local governments and tourism agencies (from nonprofit-payments), its foundation, and links to its member directory, events and join page. entity_id is its profile (entity-profiles). Chambers are private, member-owned nonprofits, not government agencies.

Columns: place_id, chamber_id, name, short_name, legal_name, entity_id, page_url, ein, sunbiz_doc_number, tax_status, founded, serves, tagline, about, mission, board_meets, board_seats, staff_listed, latest_return_year, latest_return_form, revenue, expenses, assets, employees, public_money_total, public_money_from, foundation_name, foundation_entity_id, foundation_revenue, website, events_url, directory_url, join_url, board_url, staff_url, as_of, source_url, gov_id

### Chambers of commerce: boards and staff (chamber-leaders)
Each chamber's board (executive committee, directors, ex officio and honorary members), staff and past chairs since 2016, as listed on the chamber's own website on as_of: name, title and the organization each board member represents. No phone numbers, emails or addresses. person_entity_id and organization_entity_id link to profiles; person_match and organization_match say how each link was made (blank = no match, shown as plain text).

Upcoming events from each chamber's public calendar (kind event: title, start and end in local time, venue and city, category, the event's own link) and each chamber's yearly and monthly signature programs (kind program: schedule and what it is). chamber_event is false for community events a chamber lists on its calendar. Refreshed daily where the calendar has a public feed.
Rows: 56. Columns: place_id, chamber_id, chamber, kind, sort_order, title, schedule, about, starts, ends, all_day, venue, city, category, chamber_event, cost, event_id, url, source_url, gov_id

### Community events (community-events)
What's happening around the county in the next two months, from public calendars: the county and city calendars, the library system, visitor bureaus and the Panama City Beach Chamber. One row per event date: title, start and end in local time, town, venue name, category (Community, Public meeting, Library, Chamber), recurring for programs listed on two or more dates, and the event's own link. Refreshed daily. same_as is set on a row that repeats another (the same post listed twice; it names the row kept for it) and first_posted on a kept row that was posted more than once; pages and apps show the kept rows only.
Rows: 187. Columns: place_id, event_id, source_id, source, gov, town, title, starts, ends, all_day, venue, category, recurring, cost, url, source_url, same_as, first_posted, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/community-events.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/community-events.json

### Beach access points (beach-access)
Every public beach access on the Gulf in the county from the county's GIS: name and number, street address, area (Panama City Beach, Mexico Beach or unincorporated), map point, whether cars can drive on, and whether it is wheelchair accessible (from Panama City Beach's GIS). Parking, restrooms, showers, lifeguards and boardwalks come from the Florida DEP coastal access survey where its site is within about 200 feet (state_site_id); blank means not surveyed.
Rows: 152. Columns: place_id, access_id, name, number, address, area, latitude, longitude, vehicle_access, wheelchair_access, parking, parking_spaces, ada_parking, restroom, shower, lifeguard, boardwalk, notes, state_access_name, state_site_id, source_url, run_by, gov_id

### Beach water quality: sampling sites (beach-water-sites)
Each Florida Healthy Beaches Program sampling site in the county (Florida Department of Health), with its latest rated sample, the number of Good, Moderate and Poor samples since first_date, and how many came with a health advisory. Ratings: Good 0-35, Moderate 35.5-70, Poor 70.5 or more enterococci per 100 mL of water.
Rows: 16. Columns: place_id, site_id, name, active, epa_beach_id, latitude, longitude, latest_date, latest_enterococcus, latest_rating, latest_advisory, samples, first_date, good, moderate, poor, advisories, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/beach-water-sites.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/beach-water-sites.json

### Beach water quality: samples (beach-water-samples)
Every published Healthy Beaches sample at each site: date, enterococcus count per 100 mL, the state's rating and whether a health advisory was issued. The state's lookup shows the latest 50 samples per site; samples are kept here as they come in, so history grows from 2026 on.
Rows: 732. Columns: place_id, site_id, site, sample_number, date, enterococcus, reported, advisory, rating, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/beach-water-samples.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/beach-water-samples.json

### Beach conditions and flags (beach-conditions)
From the National Weather Service Tallahassee surf zone forecast for the county's coast: kind forecast is one row per forecast period (rip current risk, surf height, UV index, water temperature, weather, winds, sunrise and sunset), the first carrying the beach flag color the beach officials reported to the weather service; kind alert is an active beach or coastal alert; kind flag is the flag color reported each day since we began recording; kind legend is what each flag color means. Refreshed daily.
Rows: 11. Columns: place_id, zone, issued, period, flag_color, meaning, rip_current_risk, surf_height, uv_index, water_temperature, weather, high_temperature, winds, sunrise, sunset, summary, date, ends, sort_order, source_url, kind, gov_id

### Development projects (development-projects)
Development projects on each local government's public planning map: Bay County's development orders for the unincorporated county (site plans for commercial buildings, subdivisions, apartments and other projects, from application to approval) and Panama City Beach's development map. One row per project: name, what it is, size, address, status and the application, approval, building permit and occupancy dates on record. Projects with no date, or nothing since 2016, are left out. Owners and developers are not listed on the maps.
Rows: 245. Columns: place_id, project_id, gov_id, government, name, case_number, description, size, location, status, applied_date, approved_date, permit_date, occupancy_date, plans_url, lat, lng, source, source_page, fetched, source_url
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/development-projects.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/development-projects.json

### New homes permitted (housing-permits)
New privately owned homes authorized by building permits, per year, for the whole county, each city and the unincorporated area, from the U.S. Census Bureau's Building Permits Survey: single-family homes, homes in 2 to 4 unit buildings and in buildings with 5 or more units, with the construction value the permits list and a one-line summary. year_to_date rows cover this year so far (period). estimated is true when the government sent the Census Bureau no monthly reports that year and the figures are the Bureau's estimate.
Rows: 99. Columns: place_id, area_id, gov_id, area, year, period, months, year_to_date, months_reported, estimated, single_family_units, single_family_value, two_to_four_units, two_to_four_buildings, two_to_four_value, five_plus_units, five_plus_buildings, five_plus_value, total_units, total_value, source_url, summary
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/housing-permits.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/housing-permits.json

### State road contracts (road-contracts)
Every Florida Department of Transportation construction and maintenance contract in the county that was under way in 2016 or later: what and where, the contractor, the current contract amount, letting, start, estimated finish and final acceptance dates, and status. status is Under way when FDOT's map shows the contract active. vendor_id links a contractor that local governments also paid. project_id is FDOT's item and segment number, which joins road-work-program.
Rows: 85. Columns: place_id, agency, contract_id, project_id, description, description_fdot, contract_type, contract_type_code, status, active_on_fdot_map, contractor, amount, let_date, executed_date, work_began_date, estimated_completion_date, final_acceptance_date, ended_date, bid_days, length_miles, lat, lng, district, website, data_date, source_url, financial_projects, roads, fetched, vendor_id, vendor_ids, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/road-contracts.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/road-contracts.json

### State road work program (road-work-program)
Projects in the Florida Department of Transportation's current adopted five-year work program in the county, one row per project and phase (planning, project development and environment study, design, right of way, construction, construction inspection): what and where, the kind of work, the fiscal years the phase is funded in (July to June, named for the year it ends) and the project's status. FDOT's map layers don't carry dollar amounts; contract amounts are in road-contracts.
Rows: 143. Columns: place_id, agency, project_id, phase_code, phase, description, description_fdot, work_type, project_status, length_miles, district, source_url, fiscal_years, first_fiscal_year, last_fiscal_year, fetched, gov_id

### Public schools (schools)
One row per public school in the district, open now or closed since 2016: state school number (school_id, district-school), federal id, level, grades taught, district or charter, address and phone of the school building, enrollment and teachers for the latest federal school directory year, students per teacher, share of students eligible for free or reduced-price lunch, latest state school grade and the one before it, latest per-student spending, and which attendance zone levels feed it. operator_entity_id is the nonprofit that runs a charter school (entity-profiles).
Rows: 59. Columns: place_id, school_id, nces_id, name, status, level, school_type, grades, charter, virtual, operator_entity_id, address, city, zip, phone, latitude, longitude, enrollment, enrollment_year, last_year_open, teachers_fte, students_per_teacher, free_reduced_lunch_pct, latest_grade, latest_grade_year, prior_grade, grades_on_record, latest_per_student, latest_spending_year, zoned_levels, district, page_url, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/schools.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/schools.json

### School grades (school-grades)
Every Florida school grade (A to F, or I for incomplete) on record for each school since 2016, from the Florida Department of Education's school grades file, one row per school and year. year is the school year's end (2025 = 2024-25). school_type is Elementary, Middle, High or Combination. Components (percent of students: third-grade reading (grade3_ela_achievement), English and math achievement and learning gains, science, social studies, acceleration, graduation rate; total points and percent of points) are filled in for each year whose state file was read (the latest two). No grades were given for 2019-20 (testing was canceled); 2020-21 grades were only given to schools that asked; 2022-23 grades were an informational baseline (informational_baseline true).
Rows: 343. Columns: place_id, school_id, school, year, school_year, grade, informational_baseline, school_type, grade3_ela_achievement, ela_achievement, ela_gains, ela_gains_low25, math_achievement, math_gains, math_gains_low25, science_achievement, social_studies_achievement, middle_acceleration, graduation_rate, college_career_acceleration, total_points, percent_of_points, percent_tested, pct_economically_disadvantaged, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/school-grades.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/school-grades.json

### School grades statewide (school-grade-state)
Florida-wide school grade results by school type (Elementary, Middle, High, Combination, and All), one row per school type and year, worked out from the Florida Department of Education's statewide school grades file: how many schools got each grade (grade_a to grade_i) and the average of each grade component across the state's schools (simple average of schools, not weighted by students). Used to compare a school with the state.
Rows: 10. Columns: state, year, school_year, school_type, schools_graded, grade_a, grade_b, grade_c, grade_d, grade_f, grade_i, grade3_ela_achievement, ela_achievement, ela_gains, ela_gains_low25, math_achievement, math_gains, math_gains_low25, science_achievement, social_studies_achievement, middle_acceleration, graduation_rate, college_career_acceleration, percent_of_points, percent_tested, pct_economically_disadvantaged, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/school-grade-state.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/school-grade-state.json

### School start and end times (school-bell-times)
When each public school's day starts and ends this school year (24-hour HH:MM), from the district's published start and end times chart, typed in by hand. Some schools have more than one row: different grade bands (part), a zero period, or a shorter Friday (note). Rows with kind 'early release' give the dismissal time by school level on early release days. school_id is empty for programs that aren't in the federal school directory.
Rows: 55. Columns: place_id, school_id, school, part, kind, start_time, end_time, note, group_name, school_year, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/school-bell-times.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/school-bell-times.json

### Spending per school (school-spending)
Per-student spending at each school from the Florida Department of Education's yearly Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA) per-pupil expenditure reports: federal, state and local, and total, one row per school and year (year = the school year's end). estimated_total multiplies the per-student figure by that year's enrollment from the federal school directory, so it is an estimate, not a reported total.
Rows: 352. Columns: place_id, school_id, school, year, school_year, federal_per_student, state_local_per_student, total_per_student, enrollment, estimated_total, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/school-spending.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/school-spending.json

### School enrollment by year (school-enrollment)
Students enrolled at each public school each school year since 2015-16 (year = the school year's end), from the U.S. Department of Education's Common Core of Data school directory.
Rows: 486. Columns: place_id, school_id, school, year, school_year, enrollment, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/school-enrollment.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/school-enrollment.json

### School district calendar (school-calendar)
The school district's calendar as posted on its website: first and last day, holidays and breaks, no-school days, early release days, end of each grading period, graduations and School Board meetings. kind is first-day, last-day, no-school, break, early-release, grading, graduation, board-meeting or other. starts and ends are local dates (all_day) or local date and time. Refreshed daily; past events of the school year stay on file.

### School attendance zones (school-zones)
The school district's attendance zones (which elementary, middle and high school serves each part of the county), from the county GIS server, one row per zone with the school it feeds (school_id), area in square miles, the county's last edit date and the zone's shape as GeoJSON (geometry, longitude/latitude, simplified to about 40 meters). mou_area marks zones the county map labels MOU (covered by a separate agreement). Choice, magnet and charter schools take students from outside their zone.
Rows: 36. Columns: place_id, zone_id, level, zone_name, school_id, school, mou_area, pieces, area_sq_mi, last_edited, geometry, source_url, gov_id

### Hurricane evacuation zones (evacuation-zones)
Bay County's hurricane evacuation zones A to D, in the order they are usually called: where each zone is, when it is ordered and what to do, with each zone's shape (geometry, GeoJSON in WGS84, simplified to about 300 m; the county map is the authority). Look up the zone for an address at /api/v1/evacuation-zone.
Rows: 4. Columns: place_id, zone, sort_order, color, where_it_is, when_ordered, plain, zone_edited, geometry, map_url, layer_url, as_of, source_url, gov_id

### Emergency shelters (emergency-shelters)
Every disaster shelter Bay County Emergency Services lists: special needs, general population, mass care support, recovery and extreme-weather shelters, with the address, the group's open or closed status as the county last posted it (status_as_of), the map point and the evacuation zone the shelter sits in. Not every shelter opens for every storm. The live status is in /api/v1/emergency.
Rows: 8. Columns: place_id, shelter_id, name, address, shelter_type, group_name, group_about, note, status, status_as_of, lat, lng, evacuation_zone, operator, source_url, checked, gov_id

### Emergency phone numbers and sign-ups (emergency-resources)
The numbers, sign-ups, maps and outage pages people need before and during an emergency, from each organization's own site: 911, the county Emergency Operations Center, AlertBay, the special needs registry, weather offices, FL511 and power outage maps.
Rows: 16. Columns: place_id, sort_order, resource_id, group, name, org, phone, url, about, gov_id, as_of, source_url

### Emergency notices archive (emergency-notices)
Every emergency notice BayCounty.me has recorded for the county, newest first: National Weather Service watches, warnings and advisories, boil-water notices, road closures, water and sewer outages, evacuation orders, shelter openings and storm updates from each government's alert center and news feed, and FL511 state road closures. kind is the topic, status active (live at the last check), ended or lifted. first_seen and last_seen are when BayCounty.me saw it. The live list is /api/v1/emergency. same_as is set on a row that repeats another (the same post listed twice; it names the row kept for it) and first_posted on a kept row that was posted more than once; pages and apps show the kept rows only.
Rows: 58. Columns: notice_id, place_id, kind, source, source_type, gov_id, title, summary, instruction, severity, event, area, zones, issued, starts, ends, updated, status, full_closure, roadway, first_seen, last_seen, url, source_url, same_as, first_posted

### Hurricane prep steps (hurricane-prep)
Plain-English steps for hurricane season, sandbags, generator safety, an approaching storm and the days after, each with the agency it comes from (Bay County, Ready.gov, CDC, National Weather Service, FEMA, the Army Corps of Engineers).
Rows: 16. Columns: place_id, sort_order, topic, step, text, source, as_of, source_url, gov_id

### Disaster declarations (disaster-declarations)
Every federal major disaster, emergency and fire management declaration that included the county since 2016, from OpenFEMA: the storm or event, the dates, and which FEMA programs were opened (individual aid to households, public aid to governments, hazard mitigation).
Rows: 20. Columns: place_id, disaster_number, title, kind, incident_type, declared, began, ended, individual_aid, public_aid, mitigation, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/disaster-declarations.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/disaster-declarations.json

### Rebuild money by ZIP code (rebuild-money)
Money that reached each ZIP code after storms since 2016, from OpenFEMA: FEMA housing aid to owners and renters (Individuals and Households Program: households that applied, approved, dollars, of which repair and rental help, and FEMA-inspected damage for owners) and flood insurance claims paid (NFIP, building, contents and compliance payments added). One row per ZIP, program and storm. Totals only; FEMA does not publish who received aid and neither does BayCounty.me.
Rows: 179. Columns: place_id, zip, area_name, program, disaster_number, event, year, count, count_label, approved, amount_paid, repair_amount, rental_amount, inspected_damage, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/rebuild-money.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/rebuild-money.json

### Elections since 2016 (elections)
Every election the Bay County Supervisor of Elections has held since 2016, one row each: the date, name and kind (primary, general, municipal, runoff, referendum, recall, presidential preference primary), registered voters, ballots cast, turnout and precincts reporting. status is final (completely reported), counting (results still coming in) or canceled. A city's own view of a municipal election day and the 2018 recounts are folded into the countywide election. Contest results are in election-results.
Rows: 33. Columns: place_id, election_id, date, name, kind, status, registered_voters, ballots_cast, turnout_pct, precincts_reporting, precincts_total, contests, updated, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/elections.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/elections.json

### Election results since 2016 (election-results)
Official results of every contest on a Bay County ballot since 2016, one row per choice: votes on Election Day, in early voting and by mail, the total and percent, and rank in the contest. level is Federal, State, Court, County, School district, City, Special district or Party; gov_id is the local government a contest elects or decides. measure is true for a yes-or-no ballot question. party_primary is REP or DEM for a closed party primary, or Universal primary when every voter could vote. recount is true where the 2018 recount figures replace the first count. person_entity_id links a local candidate to their profile. A blank vote count is 1 to 29 votes, which the law keeps from being reported for privacy. From the Supervisor of Elections' election results site.
Rows: 825. Columns: place_id, election_id, election_date, election_name, election_kind, contest_id, contest, office, level, gov_id, measure, party_primary, recount, choice, party, person_entity_id, election_day, early_voting, vote_by_mail, votes, pct, rank, over_votes, under_votes, source_url
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/election-results.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/election-results.json

### Election dates (election-dates)
Key dates for Bay County elections: registration deadlines, early voting, vote-by-mail request and return deadlines and election days (kept by hand from the Supervisor of Elections' voter guide), plus the upcoming events on the Supervisor of Elections' calendar (canvassing board meetings, tests of the voting equipment), read daily. kind says which; starts_at is the start time when one is given.
Rows: 12. Columns: place_id, date, end_date, starts_at, election, kind, title, source, url, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/election-dates.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/election-dates.json

### Where to vote (voting-locations)
Every early voting site for the next countywide election (kind early_voting: any registered Bay County voter can vote at any of them, with the dates and hours) and the Election Day polling place for each of the county's precincts (kind polling_place: on Election Day you vote only at your own precinct's polling place). lat and lon place each on a map, from Bay County's address points. From the Supervisor of Elections.
Rows: 38. Columns: place_id, kind, election, starts, ends, hours, precinct, name, address, city, zip, lat, lon, url, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/voting-locations.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/voting-locations.json

### Public notices (public-notices)
Legal notices published by local governments and public agencies on the county's public notice website: bid and proposal requests, public hearings and ordinances, public meetings and other notices, with the government that posted it (gov_id, blank for agencies that are not one of the county's local governments), the date it was published, the first date it mentions after that (the meeting, hearing or bid due date) and the full text. Court, foreclosure, tax deed, probate and other private notices on the same site are left out. The site keeps 30 days; notices already on file stay as an archive. same_as is set on a row that repeats another (the same post listed twice; it names the row kept for it) and first_posted on a kept row that was posted more than once; pages and apps show the kept rows only. The text has a blank line between paragraphs. reference is the bid, RFQ, ordinance or resolution number found in it; emails, phones and links list every email address, phone number and web address in it, separated by semicolons.
Rows: 107. Columns: place_id, notice_id, published, gov_id, agency, kind, kind_label, title, event_date, notice_type, text, pdf_url, publication, source_url, same_as, first_posted, reference, emails, phones, links
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/public-notices.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/public-notices.json

### Government job openings (job-openings)
Open jobs posted by Bay County, Bay District Schools, the cities and the airport on their own job boards, read daily: title, department, job type, pay where posted, posting and closing dates and the link to apply. Jobs whose closing date has passed are left out. first_seen is the first day the job was on file. same_as is set on a row that repeats another (the same post listed twice; it names the row kept for it) and first_posted on a kept row that was posted more than once; pages and apps show the kept rows only.
Rows: 122. Columns: place_id, job_id, board, gov_id, employer, title, department, job_type, pay, posted, closes, ref, url, first_seen, source_url, same_as, first_posted
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/job-openings.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/job-openings.json

### Government job boards (job-boards)
Each local government's job board and whether its openings are read automatically: openings is how many are open now, blank where the board cannot be read (note says why and where to look).
Rows: 10. Columns: place_id, board, gov_id, employer, url, read, openings, note, checked
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/job-boards.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/job-boards.json

### Utilities: who provides each service (utility-providers)
Who provides water, sewer, electricity, natural gas, garbage, yard waste, recycling and internet in each part of the county (area: a city, unincorporated, or all for countywide providers): the provider, what kind of provider it is, whether it covers all, most or some of the area, its phone number, website and outage page, and notes on how the service works. entity_id is the provider's profile (entity-profiles) where there is one. /api/v1/utilities?lat=&lon= picks the rows for one address.
Rows: 40. Columns: place_id, area, area_name, gov_id, service, service_label, provider, entity_id, entity_name, provider_kind, coverage, phone, website, outage_url, notes, as_of, source_url

Monthly charges set by each public utility, one row per charge: water and sewer base and usage charges (inside and outside the city, senior rates, meter sizes), garbage and stormwater on the city bill, franchise fees and utility taxes, landfill fees, and a typical monthly bill at 5,000 gallons with its arithmetic in notes, plus the same bill split into water and sewer, garbage and other charges. effective says which rate schedule the row comes from.

### Trash pickup: routes and days (trash-pickup)
Garbage, yard waste and bulk pickup in each city: one row per route with its usual pickup days, or the rule where a city has no route map (for example a private hauler sets the day). lookup_layer is the public map layer that holds the routes, zone_field the route field and day_field the day field; /api/v1/utilities?lat=&lon= reads them at an address. zone_area describes a route in words where there is no map.

### Trash pickup: holiday changes (trash-holidays)
How each city's garbage and yard waste pickup changes on holidays, as the city or its hauler publishes it: the holiday, when it falls, and what happens to garbage and yard waste pickup.
Rows: 20. Columns: place_id, area, area_name, gov_id, provider, holiday, when_observed, garbage, yard_waste, as_of, source_url
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/trash-holidays.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/trash-holidays.json

### Restaurants and food service (restaurants)
One row per restaurant, food truck, caterer or other food service license in the county: today's state license list plus every license inspected since 2016 that is no longer listed (licensed_now false). Name, kind, license holder (licensee, linked to its profile through licensee_entity_id when it matches a company or Sunbiz filing; a person is named only when their name and the license address match an officer, manager or registered agent of a registered business), location (city and ZIP only for food trucks, caterers and event vendors, whose license address can be a home), seats, when it opened (its first licensing inspection), and its inspection record: the latest result, the latest routine inspection, inspections and high-priority violations in the last 12 months, emergency closures, the results of the last six inspections (recent_results, newest first) and its page on the site (page_url). From the Florida DBPR Division of Hotels and Restaurants.
Rows: 1,440. Columns: place_id, license_number, license_type, kind, business_name, licensee, licensee_entity_id, address, city, zip, seats, licensed_now, license_expires, risk_level, opened, first_inspection, last_inspection, last_result, last_result_level, last_high_priority, last_routine_date, last_routine_violations, last_routine_high_priority, inspections, inspections_last_year, high_priority_last_year, closures, last_closure, recent_results, page_url, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/restaurants.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/restaurants.json

### Restaurant inspections (restaurant-inspections)
Every state food safety inspection of a restaurant, food truck, caterer or other food service license in the county since 2016, one row per visit: date, type (routine, complaint, licensing, or a follow-up visit when visit_number is over 1), the state's disposition and what it means in plain words (result, result_level ok, warning, fine or closed), violation counts by priority (high priority violations are the ones most likely to make someone sick), and the violation items cited. From the Florida DBPR Division of Hotels and Restaurants public records, refreshed daily.
Rows: 17,215. Columns: place_id, visit_id, license_number, business_name, city, date, inspection_type, visit_number, disposition, result, result_level, high_priority, intermediate, basic, total_violations, violation_codes, violation_items, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/restaurant-inspections.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/restaurant-inspections.json

### New businesses (new-businesses)
Every company, nonprofit and partnership filed with the Florida Division of Corporations (Sunbiz) since 2016 whose main address is in the county, newest first: name, type, filing date, whether it is still active, city and ZIP (street addresses are left out because many small companies list a home), its latest annual report, its profile id, any restaurant it holds a license for, and a link to its state record, which names its officers and registered agent. Out-of-state companies count from the day they registered to do business in Florida. Updated when the state publishes its quarterly corporate file.
Rows: 41,946. Columns: place_id, doc_number, name, filing_type, filed_date, filed_month, status, city, zip, last_filing_date, latest_annual_report, entity_id, restaurants, source_url, gov_id

### This week in Bay County (weekly-roundup)
This week's edition of the weekly email and the /this-week page, one row per item: events happening this week (one-off events first; repeating programs and meetings left out), public meetings this week, and votes, contracts and change orders that first appeared on BayCounty.me last week (first_seen; minutes come out weeks after a meeting, so date can be earlier). section is event, meeting, vote, contract or change_order; featured marks what the email shows. people lists who voted no, with profile links. Rebuilt every morning.
Rows: 125. Columns: place_id, week_of, section, rank, featured, record_id, title, summary, date, starts, ends, all_day, gov_id, government, board, town, venue, category, recurring, agenda_posted, amount, new_total, method, outcome, tally, split, voted_no, people, vendor, vendor_entity_id, vendor_url, url, page_url, source, source_url, first_seen
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/weekly-roundup.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/weekly-roundup.json

### Military installations (military-installations)
One row per military base in the county: branch, host unit, commander (with the change-of-command story that names them), mission, main tenant commands, size and history, its website and DVIDS page, and how many news stories are on file. Hand-checked from the units' own stories and public base histories; commanders change every two to three years.
Rows: 2. Columns: place_id, installation_id, name, short_name, branch, host_unit, commander, commander_title, commander_since, commander_source_url, location, opened, acres, personnel, mission, storm, tenants, website, dvids_url, news_units, stories, latest_story, as_of, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/military-installations.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/military-installations.json

### Military news from the bases (military-news)
News stories published by the public affairs offices of the units at Tyndall Air Force Base and Naval Support Activity Panama City (325th Fighter Wing, 601st Air and Space Operations Center, NSA Panama City, Naval Surface Warfare Center Panama City Division, Navy Experimental Diving Unit), read daily from each unit's DVIDS feed: title, summary, date (Central time), author and the story's own link. Story text and photos stay on DVIDS. 2016 and later.
Rows: 43. Columns: place_id, news_id, installation_id, installation, unit, unit_id, title, summary, published, author, url, image_url, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/military-news.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/military-news.json

### Federal contracts to local companies (federal-contracts)
Every federal contract with money obligated since 2016 to a company whose business address is in the county, from USAspending.gov: recipient (as registered in SAM.gov, with its city, never its street address), the agency and branch that signed it, what it buys (description, industry and product codes), start and end dates, and obligated, the money obligated from 2016 on (modifications and cuts included, so it can be negative). award_amount is USAspending's lifetime total, which can include earlier years. defense is true for Department of Defense contracts. recipient_entity_id links to the company's profile; recipient_match says how it was joined to other records (blank: by its own name only).
Rows: 6,425. Columns: place_id, award_key, award_id, recipient, recipient_uei, recipient_city, recipient_entity_id, recipient_url, recipient_match, agency, sub_agency, agency_entity_id, defense, award_type, description, naics, naics_description, psc, psc_description, start_date, end_date, first_action_date, last_action_date, actions, obligated, award_amount, performance_city, performance_county, performance_state, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/federal-contracts.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/federal-contracts.json

### Federal contracts to local companies by year (federal-contract-years)
Money obligated each calendar year since 2016 on federal contracts to companies based in the county, per company and signing agency, from USAspending.gov contract transactions: obligated dollars, number of contract actions and number of contracts.
Rows: 1,431. Columns: place_id, year, recipient, recipient_entity_id, recipient_url, agency, sub_agency, agency_entity_id, defense, obligated, actions, awards, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/federal-contract-years.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/federal-contract-years.json

### Tax districts (tax-districts)
Which taxing authorities levy property tax in each tax district, and the combined millage. Rates by year are in property-tax-rates (authority_id).
Rows: 10. Columns: district, label, authority_ids, total_millage, tax_district_codes, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/tax-districts.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/tax-districts.json

### Police and fire departments (safety-agencies)
Who polices and who fights fires in each local government: the agency, how it is arranged (own department, the Sheriff, or a city paying the Sheriff by contract), the FY2026 budget for it (budget_lines names the lines added from the government's adopted budget, the same figures as the budget pages), cost_per_resident (the budget over residents: the city's population; the whole county for the Sheriff, who runs the jail for everyone; the unincorporated county for county fire), the latest sworn officers and civilian staff the agency reported to the FBI, and its FBI reporting number (fbi_ori). Hand-checked.
Rows: 16. Columns: place_id, agency_id, agency, service, gov_id, government, agency_gov_id, arrangement, budget_amount, budget_lines, budget_fiscal_year, budget_source_url, residents, cost_per_resident, fbi_ori, officers, civilians, staffing_year, website, source_url
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/safety-agencies.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/safety-agencies.json

### Crimes reported by police agency (crime-counts)
Offenses each police agency in the county reported to the FBI's Uniform Crime Reporting program each year since 2016, from the FBI Crime Data Explorer: violent and property crime totals (total_row true) and murder, rape, robbery, aggravated assault, burglary, larceny-theft, motor vehicle theft and arson, with offenses cleared (solved or closed), the population the agency covers, and the statewide rate for the same offense and year (florida_per_1000; blank for 2021, when only half of Florida reported). A missing year means the agency sent nothing that year (no Florida agency reported for 2021; Panama City Beach has not reported since 2020). Florida agencies sent one yearly summary until 2024 and monthly incident reports (NIBRS) from 2025, so 2025 on is not directly comparable with earlier years. months_reported below 12 means the year is partial; per_1000 is left blank then. Counts only; no person is named.
Rows: 580. Columns: place_id, agency_id, agency, fbi_ori, gov_id, year, offense_code, offense, offense_group, total_row, count, cleared, months_reported, population, per_1000, florida_per_1000, reporting, source_url
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/crime-counts.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/crime-counts.json

### Crimes reported by police agency, by month (crime-monthly)
Offenses each police agency in the county reported to the FBI each month since January 2025, when Florida agencies moved to monthly incident reports (NIBRS), from the FBI Crime Data Explorer: violent and property crime totals (total_row true) and the eight main offenses, with offenses cleared. This is where this year's numbers come from before the year is over: the page compares this year so far with the same months last year, leaving out the current month and the two before it, which agencies are still adding to. A month that is missing has not been sent yet. Counts only; no person is named.
Rows: 1,040. Columns: place_id, agency_id, agency, fbi_ori, gov_id, year, month, period, offense_code, offense, offense_group, total_row, count, cleared, source_url
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/crime-monthly.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/crime-monthly.json

### Police staffing (police-staffing)
Sworn officers and civilian employees at each police agency in the county on October 31 each year since 2016, as the agency reported them to the FBI (Crime Data Explorer police employee data), with employees per 1,000 residents covered. The Sheriff's reported civilian staff went from 71 in 2022 to 271 in 2023; the FBI data does not say why.
Rows: 54. Columns: place_id, agency_id, agency, fbi_ori, gov_id, year, officers, civilians, employees, female_officers, employees_per_1000, population, source_url
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/police-staffing.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/police-staffing.json

### How current each figure is (data-freshness)
One row per headline figure on the site: the newest period we have (latest_period, read from the data itself so it moves as refreshes bring in more), whether that is this year, this year so far, the newest the source has published, or newer data that needs a by-hand download (status), when the next period is usually published (next_due, the source's usual schedule as checked on checked_on, not a promise), how we get it, and the source.
Rows: 14. Columns: topic, figure, page, latest_period, latest_year, status, next_due, how_we_get_it, source, source_url, notes, checked_on, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/data-freshness.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/data-freshness.json

### Volunteer needs (volunteer-needs)
Open volunteer needs in the county, read every day from public volunteer boards (United Way of Northwest Florida's volunteer center and Idealist): what volunteers do, the organization, a plain cause, when (ongoing, one day or shifts), the city and ZIP, and the board's sign-up link. nonprofit_id and organization_entity_id link to the local nonprofit's profile where the name matches. No street addresses or contact details.
Rows: 18. Columns: place_id, need_id, title, organization, nonprofit_id, organization_entity_id, organization_url, cause, board_interest, schedule, when_text, starts, ends, posted, closes, first_seen, description, details, city, zip, remote, board, url, as_of, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/volunteer-needs.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/volunteer-needs.json

### Nonprofits that use volunteers (volunteer-orgs)
Local nonprofits that reported volunteers on their latest IRS Form 990 (Part I line 6, the organization's own estimate, which can cover more than this county) or that have a volunteer need open now: what each does, a plain cause, website, volunteers and employees reported, revenue, and open needs. Homeowner associations, chambers and private foundations are left out unless they post a need.
Rows: 76. Columns: place_id, nonprofit_id, entity_id, page_url, name, cause, kind, city, mission, website, volunteers_reported, volunteers_year, employees, revenue, open_needs, needs_boards, latest_return_form, latest_return_year, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/volunteer-orgs.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/volunteer-orgs.json

### Votes that name a company or organization (vote-mentions)
One row per recorded vote and each company, nonprofit or registered business its motion names, matched by name from the minutes (hand-researched votes and every vote read from minutes since 2016): the vote, the organization and its profile (entity_id), the words that matched, the roll call (roll_call, 'Name: vote' pairs) and the members' profile ids (member_ids). A match means the minutes name the organization in that motion; consent agendas name many items in one vote.
Rows: 1,373. Columns: place_id, vote_id, date, gov_id, board, entity_id, entity_name, entity_kind, entity_url, matched_words, headline, agenda_item, category, amount, outcome, tally, consent_agenda, roll_call, member_ids, source_type, source_url
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/vote-mentions.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/vote-mentions.json

### Votes on motions naming a member's donor (donor-votes)
One row per member vote on a motion that names a company which gave to that member's campaign (donor_kind company) or whose owner gave personally (donor_kind business owner; owners are named only when their name and address match a Sunbiz officer, manager or registered agent). With the gift total, the first and last gift dates and whether the gifts came before or after the vote. A gift near a vote does not show why anyone voted the way they did. Individual donors are never named.
Rows: 571. Columns: place_id, vote_id, date, gov_id, board, member, member_id, member_url, member_vote, donor, donor_id, donor_url, donor_kind, company, company_id, company_url, gift_amount, gift_first_date, gift_last_date, gift_timing, headline, amount, outcome, tally, consent_agenda, source_type, source_url, report_url
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/donor-votes.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/donor-votes.json

### Companies and organizations on agendas (agenda-parties)
One row per company, organization or government named on a board's agenda (agenda items read from the published agenda packets), linked to its profile where the name matches, with any campaign gifts from it (or from the owners who run it) to people who serve that government (gave_to_members, gave_to). rezoning is true for rezoning and land-use items.
Rows: 526. Columns: place_id, gov_id, board, meeting_date, meeting, item_number, title, kind, rezoning, amount, party, entity_id, entity_name, entity_kind, entity_url, gave_to_members, gave_to, source_url
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/agenda-parties.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/agenda-parties.json

### Development projects and the businesses behind them (development-companies)
Development projects on the county and city planning maps whose name is exactly the name of one active Bay County business filing (Sunbiz), with that business's payments from the same government and campaign gifts from it or its owners to that government's officials. The maps don't list owners or developers, so only projects named after their business are matched.
Rows: 11. Columns: place_id, project_id, project, gov_id, description, status, applied_date, approved_date, company, company_id, company_url, sunbiz_doc_number, match, paid_by_this_government, gave_to_members, gave_to, source_url
