### Bids from notice to award (bid-trail)
Each bid or proposal request in the public notices, followed by its bid number to the recorded votes and contract records (awards, change orders, emergency purchases) at the same government that carry the same number: one row per step (stage notice, vote, award, change order), oldest notice last.
Rows: 11. Columns: place_id, notice_id, reference, gov_id, agency, published, due_date, notice_title, notice_url, stage, date, what, vendor, vendor_id, amount, outcome, source_url
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/bid-trail.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/bid-trail.json

### Companies paid by one government that share an officer (shared-owner-vendors)
Companies paid by the same local government that list the same person (same name and Sunbiz address) as an officer or manager, one row per company, government and shared person. Registered agents are left out. Sharing an officer is common among related companies and is not a finding of wrongdoing.
Rows: 14. Columns: place_id, group_id, gov_id, officer, company, company_id, company_url, sunbiz_doc_number, paid_by_this_government, companies_in_group, match, source_url

### Chamber board members who are donors, vendors or officials (chamber-overlaps)
Chamber of commerce board members and staff (chamber-leaders) whose company is paid by a local government or gave to a local campaign, who gave to a campaign themselves as a business owner, or who are elected officials. Rows with none of these are left out.
Rows: 14. Columns: place_id, chamber, chamber_entity_id, person, person_id, person_url, title, role_group, year, current, organization, organization_id, organization_url, is_official, organization_paid_by_governments, organization_gave_to_campaigns, person_gave_to_campaigns, gave_to, source_url, gov_id

### Emergency purchases and campaign gifts (emergency-purchase-donors)
Every emergency purchase (bought without the usual bidding), with campaign gifts from the company, or from the owners who run it, to people who serve the government that bought.
Rows: 12. Columns: place_id, gov_id, government, vendor, vendor_id, vendor_url, amount, date, purpose, basis, gave_to_officials_here, gave_to, source_url
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/emergency-purchase-donors.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/emergency-purchase-donors.json

### Money raised and votes won (campaign-results)
Each local candidate since 2016 with a campaign report and an official result: money raised and spent, where it came from (individuals summed, never named), votes, vote share, rank in the race by votes and by money, and cost per vote (spent / votes). Joined on election date and candidate name.
Rows: 170. Columns: place_id, election_date, election, gov_id, office, contest, candidate, person_id, outcome, total_raised, total_spent, from_businesses, from_individuals, own_money, votes, vote_pct, vote_rank, money_rank, candidates_with_reports, cost_per_vote, report_url, source_url
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/campaign-results.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/campaign-results.json

### Contract votes and their dollar figures (contract-vote-dollars)
Every recorded vote since 2016 on a contract, purchase, change order or task order, or on a consent agenda, with the dollar figure it approved and whether that figure is counted in the officials' contract-dollar totals. counted false gives not_counted_reason: no figure in the record of the vote, several figures (which one passed is not clear), a consent agenda (many items in one vote), not new spending (a credit, sale, lease, fee, payment on work already approved, grant received, rate or new total), or the same item voted on again (same_item_as is the vote that is counted). amount_from says where the figure came from: the vote summary, the motion text, or a contract record tied to the vote (contract_record_ids). up_to marks a not-to-exceed ceiling; per_year marks one year's price. Rules: site/vote_dollars.py.
Rows: 3,566. Columns: vote_id, gov_id, body, board, date, agenda_item, headline, category, kind, amount, amount_from, up_to, per_year, counted, not_counted_reason, same_item_as, outcome, tally, vote_method, verified, contract_record_ids, contract_vendor_ids, source_type, source_title, source_url, source_page
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/contract-vote-dollars.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/contract-vote-dollars.json

### Contract dollars by member vote (member-contract-dollars)
One row per board member per counted contract vote (counted true in contract-vote-dollars): how the member voted (yes, no, absent, abstain) on that dollar figure. Sum amount where vote is yes and outcome is passed for the dollars a member voted to approve.
Rows: 4,307. Columns: vote_id, person_id, member, vote, gov_id, board, date, headline, kind, amount, up_to, per_year, outcome, tally, vote_method, source_url, source_page
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/member-contract-dollars.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/member-contract-dollars.json

### Contract dollars each official voted on (contract-dollar-totals)
One row per official per government: the dollars in counted contract votes they voted yes on that passed (yes_total, yes_votes), voted yes on that failed (yes_failed_total), and voted no on (no_total, no_votes), the dates of the first and last counted vote, every contract vote they took part in (contract_votes), and how many of those are not in the totals and why (not_counted_*). Only votes with one clear dollar figure are counted, so the totals are a floor, not everything a board spent.
Rows: 101. Columns: person_id, member, gov_id, yes_total, yes_votes, yes_failed_total, yes_failed_votes, no_total, no_votes, absent_or_abstained_votes, first_date, last_date, contract_votes, not_counted_consent, not_counted_no_amount, not_counted_unclear, not_counted_not_spending, not_counted_repeat
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/contract-dollar-totals.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/contract-dollar-totals.json

### Contract votes checked against the contract list (contract-minutes-check)
Every passed contract vote read from the minutes since October 2022 (consent agendas and votes that approve no spending, such as mutual aid, interlocal agreements, terminations and rejected bids, left out), checked against the contracts dataset. status: in_list (tied to a contract, change order or emergency purchase there, contract_record_ids), under_threshold (the vote's one clear figure is below list_threshold, the smallest award the list collects for that government), after_review (the meeting is after list_reviewed_through, the last meeting date read into the list), no_amount (the minutes give no single clear dollar figure), or missing (at or above the threshold, before the review date, and not in the list). amount is the vote's one clear figure from contract-vote-dollars. checked_note explains a vote looked at by hand (for example, the minutes don't name the seller). Rules: site/contract_coverage.py.
Rows: 708. Columns: vote_id, gov_id, board, date, year, headline, kind, amount, up_to, status, checked_note, in_contract_list, contract_record_ids, list_threshold, list_reviewed_through, source_title, source_url
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/contract-minutes-check.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/contract-minutes-check.json

### Contract awards and what came after (award-follow-up)
Every passed contract award read from the minutes since 2016 (consent agendas, votes that approve no spending, and change orders, amendments and renewals left out), one row per award and company named, checked for any later record at the same government that names the same company or carries the same bid number: later votes and agenda items, contract records and change orders, check register, tourist tax and CRA payments, and project histories. status: followed_up (later_records found; later_kinds says which, first_later_* is the first one), no_follow_up (no later record by flag_after, six months after the award), too_soon (not yet six months), as_needed (no later record, but the award is a standing or on-call agreement used only when work is ordered), cant_check (the minutes name no company). company_from says whether the company matched a profile (entity_id) or is the name as the motion writes it. A no_follow_up row is a question for the government, not a finding: the work may be recorded in files the site doesn't hold. Rules: site/award_followup.py.
Rows: 1,493. Columns: vote_id, gov_id, board, award_date, year, headline, amount, bid_numbers, flag_after, source_url, entity_id, company, company_from, status, later_records, later_kinds, first_later_date, first_later_what, first_later_url, last_later_date
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/award-follow-up.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/award-follow-up.json

### Special event road closures (event-road-closures)
Road closures and traffic delays for special events such as IRONMAN Florida, one row per closure, from the police department's traffic advisory: the road and the cross streets it is closed between, closed or delay, and when it starts and ends (ISO times with the Central offset). geometry is the closed stretch as a GeoJSON line in WGS84, placed on the county street centerlines from the street names (placed = street-names).
Rows: 4. Columns: place_id, event_id, event_name, event_page, closure_id, sort_order, road, limits, kind, starts_at, ends_at, town, gov_id, geometry, placed, as_of, source, source_url
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/event-road-closures.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/event-road-closures.json

### Special event visitor guide (event-guide)
The visitor guide for each special event on the site, one row per item: the race week schedule (at = start time), the course (distance_miles), where to watch (with a map point where there is one), getting around and things to do nearby, each with its source.
Rows: 25. Columns: place_id, event_id, event_name, section, sort_order, title, text, when_text, at, distance_miles, lat, lon, link, as_of, source, source_url, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/event-guide.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/event-guide.json

### Site photos (site-photos)
Photos of places in the county on BayCounty.me's own pages, one row per spot a photo fills (page and slot: hero is the top of the homepage, door:<section> the homepage card for that menu section, feature the this-week story, money the Your money band). title says what it shows and place_name where. photo_url is the WebP BayCounty.me serves (small_path a smaller copy for cards). Picked by hand from Wikimedia Commons, free licenses only: credit is the photographer, license and license_url the license, source_url the photo's Commons page.
Rows: 7. Columns: place_id, photo_id, page, slot, title, place_name, photo_url, photo_path, small_path, credit, license, license_url, source_url, taken, fetched_on, gov_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/site-photos.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/site-photos.json

### Planning and zoning boards (planning-boards)
Each government's appointed planning board (planning commission, planning board, planning & zoning board) and board of adjustment: what it decides, who it recommends to (the commission or council makes the final decision), who appoints it, seats and terms, how many members are listed and from what record (roster_as_of, roster_source_url), the next and last meeting from the meetings dataset (board_id matches meetings.board) with agenda and minutes links, and what records the government posts online.
Rows: 9. Columns: board_id, gov_id, name, kind, also, what_it_does, recommends_to, appointed_by, seats, alternates, term_years, members_listed, roster_as_of, roster_source, roster_source_url, roster_note, records_online, next_meeting, next_meeting_status, next_agenda_url, last_meeting, last_agenda_url, last_minutes_url, page_url, source_url

### Planning and zoning board members (planning-board-members)
Who sits on each planning and zoning board: name, role (chair, vice chair, member, alternate), seat and term end where the city lists them, and who appoints the board. Members are public appointees, named because the government publishes them; no addresses, phone numbers or emails. From the city's own board page where there is one (Mexico Beach, Parker), otherwise the roll call in the board's latest posted minutes (as_of is that meeting's date). Only full names are listed. person_entity_id links to the member's profile; person_match is 'official' when the member is also a local official.
Rows: 34. Columns: board_id, gov_id, board, sort_order, name, role, seat, term_end, appointed_by, person_entity_id, person_url, person_match, as_of, source_title, source_url
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/planning-board-members.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/planning-board-members.json

### Budget cost per resident, by service (budget-per-resident)
FY2026 General Fund budget per resident for police, fire, streets, parks, libraries, planning and administration, with the city median. Departments are grouped by name; the departments_included column shows what was added together. Schools are not included.
Rows: 64. Columns: government, kind, fiscal_year, service_id, service, general_fund_amount, residents, per_resident, city_median_per_resident, vs_city_median_pct, in_city_median, departments_included, source_url, gov_id, date_start, date_end, date_precision
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/budget-per-resident.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/budget-per-resident.json

### Budgets by fund and department (budget-detail)
Adopted budgets broken down by fund and general-fund department.

### Public salaries by job title (salary-positions)
Pay ranges, budgeted positions and unnamed actual salaries by job title for the county, constitutional officers, school district, cities, airport and port. Rows with fte_only = true are positions the source counts but gives no pay for (see pay_status).
Rows: 1,455. Columns: employer, employer_id, government, fiscal_year, title, department, category, grade, pay_min, pay_mid, pay_max, pay_basis, hourly_min, hourly_max, actual_salaries, budgeted_fte, union, source_url, notes, fte_only, pay_status, gov_id, date_start, date_end, date_precision
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/salary-positions.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/salary-positions.json

### 2026 contributions from organizations (campaign-contributions-2026)
Every contribution from a business, committee or party to a 2026 local candidate. Individual donors are not included, and neither is bank interest on campaign accounts.
Rows: 164. Columns: candidate, office, contributor, contributor_type, city, amount, date, kind, report_url, vendor_id, vendor_ids, gov_id

### Local campaigns since 2016 (campaign-history)
Every candidate who opened a campaign account with the Bay County Supervisor of Elections for a local race from 2016 through 2025, winners and losers: what each raised and spent, and how much came from individuals (summed, never named), businesses, committees, parties and the candidate. The 2026 races are in candidates-2026.
Rows: 342. Columns: election_year, election, election_date, primary_date, government, gov_id, office, candidate, party, outcome, soe_status, total_raised, monetary, in_kind, loans, total_spent, n_contributions, from_individuals_total, from_individuals_count, from_individuals_in_county, from_businesses, from_pacs_and_committees, from_parties, from_other, own_money, own_loans, reports_through, reconciliation, soe_candidate_id, report_url, source_url, person_id
CSV: https://baycounty.me/downloads/campaign-history.csv · JSON: https://baycounty.me/downloads/campaign-history.json

### Contributions from organizations, 2016-2025 (campaign-contributions-history)
Every contribution from a business, committee or party to a local candidate in the 2016 to 2025 elections, as filed. Individual donors are not included, and neither is bank interest on campaign accounts.
Rows: 2,691. Columns: election_year, election, gov_id, office, candidate, outcome, contributor, contributor_type, city, amount, date, kind, report_url, vendor_id, vendor_ids
